articles.detail: 5 cycles, 13 selected and written in every one; 4 deployed in-cycle — the 17:02 build failed and its 13 articles shipped with the 22:02 build

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, no pause gate is set, and every goal metric cleared its target — skip-if-healthy applies. Today's failures were a stale working-tree edit and two writer turn caps, neither of which any tunable parameter reaches; the one queued candidate (2026-05-08-numerical-density) edits scripts/write-prompt.md, out of scope here, so it stays queued.
weakestArea: The weakest number is not on the goal list. Daily multi-source is 18, its best reading in weeks, but the weekly rate sits at 19.3% (24.3 wk 07-19 → 19.2 wk 07-26 → 19.3 wk 08-02) and the cause is visible in the funnel: the feed supplied 4, 7, 7 and 13 multi-source stories across the four logged cycles against a historical median of 9. The selector cannot pick what clustering does not bundle, and history already records that pushing its floors twice moved rejections rather than coverage — so the lever, if one is wanted, is upstream in fetch-news-api.js source composition. Of the goal metrics proper, regional spread is thinnest: six regions clears four, but Africa fell to 4 and Oceania supplied 2, both on a handful of filings.
watching: Hormuz produced three filings in one day from different angles — Iran talks on the port blockade, Oman mediating, and a piece built entirely on the claims diverging — so the corridor is now a source-symmetry problem rather than a coverage one.

Russia's Black Sea escort expansion and the Bab el-Mandeb traffic drop are the same maritime-risk story reaching readers through two unconnected desks; watch whether they stay separate as the shipping picture consolidates.
Two 2026-08-12 eclipse articles remain filed ahead of date, carried over from yesterday's watch item — check at publication that they are not restating each other.

Ethiopia-Tigray clashes resuming, alongside Boko Haram command localization and the Nigeria USAID mortality count, is the most Africa coverage in days but rests on three unrelated filings rather than sustained attention.
Psychosis appears twice in one day from different substrates (tau markers, NLP marker variance); specialist science clustering like this is where duplicate risk usually starts.
coverageGaps: Africa fell to 4 filings, its thinnest of the week, with nothing from the Sahel beyond the Boko Haram piece and no follow-through on Sudan after yesterday's RSF thread.
Oceania reached readers through 2 filings — an Australian halal-export story and bird flu arriving in Antarctica — neither of which is Pacific reporting.
Latin America improved on yesterday's single filing (megaprison boom, Cuba's grid) but still arrives mostly through outside outlets rather than regional ones.
Science volume continues to rest on Nature and Phys.org; the remaining science slots came from general outlets covering research incidentally.
context: The busiest day of the week (62 articles, 58 unique sources, zero duplicates, top source at 13%) and also the least reliable. The 17:02 cycle wrote and validated 13 articles and published none: the build died on `public/islands/_map/starfield.ts:442 — the symbol "outer" has already been declared`, a duplicate const from an in-flight working-tree edit to the starfield. Nothing was lost — the file was fixed before 22:02 and those articles went out with that build, roughly five hours late — but a code edit sitting uncommitted on the pipeline server is a live no-publish risk, and it is worth confirming that whoever was editing the sky is done. Separately, the 08:02 and 12:02 writers exited 1 on `Reached max turns (60)`; both had already written all 13 articles and the cap only truncated the Sonnet self-revision pass, so throughput was unaffected, but two turn caps in one day suggests the writer's revision loop is running close to its ceiling. Timing was otherwise stable at 1040s (selector 286s, writer 253s, editor 85s).
